# Effect: widener

Stereo widener: increases the left/right difference for a wider sound; lows can stay mono.

**Where to put it**: Good for pad, chords, reverb bus and master bus (lightly). Keep bass, kick and lead vocal centered.

Latest parameters: `muser effects widener` (MCP: `describe_effect`)

## Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `width` | 1.5 | 0 – 2 | Width. 1 unchanged; 1.2-1.6 typical; 0 becomes mono |
| `bass_mono_hz` | 120 | 0 – 1000 Hz | Frequencies below this stay mono (lows don't spread). 0 = off |

All parameters can be omitted and take their default when omitted; when a value is out of range, `muser validate` reports the exact location.

## Minimal example

```json
{ "type": "widener", "width": 1.4, "bass_mono_hz": 150 }
```

## Scenario presets

- Widen a pad / chords

  ```json
  {"type": "widener", "width": 1.5, "bass_mono_hz": 150}
  ```

- Widen the reverb bus

  ```json
  {"type": "widener", "width": 1.3, "bass_mono_hz": 200}
  ```

- Narrow (focus one instrument)

  ```json
  {"type": "widener", "width": 0.5, "bass_mono_hz": 0}
  ```

## Tips and common mistakes

- It only works on stereo sound: a mono instrument (identical left and right) needs chorus or auto_pan first to have any 'width' to expand.
- Above width 1.6 the sound clearly thins out when summed to mono (phone speaker); on the master bus keep it at or below 1.2.
- bass_mono_hz keeps the lows in the center, so the lows are stable and powerful; 0 turns it off.
